item.title: Hegseth vows thorough probe of school strike that Trump blamed on Iran
item.summary: The announcement appeared to tacitly acknowledge a growing body of evidence that U.S. forces, not Iran, were responsible for the deadly attack.

item.title: Cuba acknowledges secret meetings with U.S. as Trump dials up threats
item.summary: Trump has warned that Cuba is next in line after Venezuela and Iran, saying that the Havana regime is in its “last moments of life.”

item.title: 6 dead after U.S. Air Force refueler crashes in Iraq while supporting Iran war
item.summary: The KC-135 tanker was involved in an apparent accident with another KC-135. The other aircraft landed safely, officials said.

item.title: Trump administration allows for Russian oil sales as energy prices soar
item.summary: The move is likely to be a boon to Russia as the United States tries to stem the economic fallout from its war on Iran as the price of crude has soared.

item.title: Unpopular war makes friendship with Trump a liability for European leaders
item.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and a constellation of other conservative leaders are the defensive over their ties to President Trump because of his war against Iran.

item.title: Lebanon appeals to Israel’s allies to intervene and says hundreds are killed
item.summary: The war is expanding into Lebanon, as an Israeli offensive to dismantle Hezbollah has displaced 800,000 people there, with more than 680 people killed.

item.title: U.S. sailors injured in fire aboard aircraft carrier supporting Iran war
item.summary: The incident, in a laundry room on the USS Gerald R. Ford, is another setback during the ship’s extended deployment.

item.title: Nations agree to release oil reserves as war in Iran hits global economy
item.summary: The International Energy Agency announced that it would carry out its largest-ever release of oil reserves — 400 million barrels.

item.title: Satellite companies restrict access to Middle East imagery amid Iran war
item.summary: The U.S.-based companies, Planet Labs and Vantor, say they were not instructed by any government to restrict image access.

item.title: Iranian school was on U.S. target list, may have been mistaken as military site
item.summary: The strike on an Iranian elementary school killed at least 175, many of them children, raising questions as to whether the military’s use of AI-enabled targeting was a factor.
